existing_ledger_row_to_preserve.evidence: Read all six steps, exact four suppliers and history-DAG procedure, and de Berg Chapter 9 pp. 204–208, Lemmas 9.11/9.13 and Theorem 9.12, including the full conflict-count argument. Temporary nodes receive at most two charges per old destroyed triangle. Harmonic summation gives expected O(n log n) walks and O(n) nodes; O(r) worst-case new nodes per stage gives O(n^3) walks. finding.evidence: The Statement says an unqualified doubling step in the algorithm “preserves $G_j,H_j\succeq0$.” The current algorithm Definition also admits finite arithmetic, where it sets $W_j=\widehat W_j$ and says: “The point certifier's solution balls are diagnostics for the stored solve and do not make the rounded recurrence an exact PSD-preserving recurrence.” The PSD and composition conclusions require the exact inverse recurrence; the Statement does not restrict to that mode.

The Statement says to “start exact mode” of the cited algorithm and claims the sequence converges to $X_*$. Its current Definition takes a “finite outer budget $N$,” runs only $j=0,\ldots,N-1$, stops if a solve does not return success, and returns after at most $N$ updates. For example, with scalar CARE data $A=B=C=R=1$, stabilizing $K_0=2$, and $N=1$, the only computed cost matrix is $X_0=5/2$, whereas $X_*=1+\sqrt2$; the finite call does not produce a sequence converging to $X_*$. The Statement needs to specify an infinite exact recurrence with successful solves, or limit its conclusion to finite prefixes.
